language.label: Language
language.@label: Settings → Appearance: the row and dropdown that choose the interface's language
language.hint: Menus, buttons and messages. The window restarts to change it.
language.@system: the language option that follows the computer's language; {language} is that language's name, e.g. English

you.title: You
you.@title: Settings: heading of the section about the person using the app (their name)
you.name: Name
you.@name: Settings → You: the row for the person's own name (what Home calls them), not the name of a thing
you.@yourName: Settings → You: placeholder and accessible name of the field for the person's own name

account.title: Account
account.@title: Settings: heading of the section about the signed-in account
account.@username: Settings → Account: the account's username written as a handle; {username} is the username
account.@usernameEmail: Settings → Account: the username as a handle, then the account's email address; {username} is the username, {email} the email address
account.@noUsernameEmail: Settings → Account: shown when the account has no username yet, then its email address; {email} is the email address
account.signedOutHint: Sign in to add friends and write together. Your notes stay on this computer.
account.@signIn: Settings → Account: button that opens the sign-in sheet

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.@title: Settings: heading of the section about how the app looks
appearance.@theme: Settings → Appearance: the row that chooses light or dark

themes.@light: Settings → Theme: option for the light look (light backgrounds)
themes.@dark: Settings → Theme: option for the dark look (dark backgrounds)
themes.@auto: Settings → Theme: option that follows the computer's light or dark setting

appearance.colorThemeHint: Backgrounds and text, in light and dark
appearance.@customTheme: Settings → Color theme: the tile for a color theme the person makes on a color wheel
appearance.ownThemeHint: Turn the wheel to choose a color, and move out toward the edge for a stronger tint. Light and dark versions are made to match, with text kept easy to read.
appearance.@tint: Settings → custom color theme: slider for how strongly the theme's color tints backgrounds and text

themeIdeas.@ocean: Settings → custom color theme: a ready-made starting point with a blue tint, named after the sea
themeIdeas.@forest: Settings → custom color theme: a ready-made starting point with a green tint
themeIdeas.@sand: Settings → custom color theme: a ready-made starting point with a warm beige tint
themeIdeas.@blush: Settings → custom color theme: a ready-made starting point with a soft pink tint
themeIdeas.@lavender: Settings → custom color theme: a ready-made starting point with a light purple tint
themeIdeas.@mint: Settings → custom color theme: a ready-made starting point with a fresh blue-green tint

appearance.@customAccent: Settings → Accent color: shown under the row when the accent was made on the color wheel; {hex} is its color code, like #4F6BED
appearance.@brightness: Settings → custom accent color: slider for how light or dark the color is
appearance.@previewButton: Settings → custom accent color: sample text on a sample button drawn in the accent color (a noun)
appearance.@previewSelected: Settings → custom accent color: sample text drawn as if it were selected, to show the selection color

fonts.@sans: Settings → Page font: the app's usual font (sans-serif)
fonts.@serif: Settings → Page font: a serif font (with small strokes at the ends of letters)
fonts.@mono: Settings → Page font: a monospaced font (every letter as wide as the next)

appearance.@fontSample: Settings → Page font: two letters drawn in each font so you can see what it looks like; use two letters typical of your script
appearance.@zoom: Settings → Appearance: the row (and its buttons) that make the whole app bigger or smaller
appearance.zoomHint: Everything bigger or smaller, also with {mod} and the scroll wheel
appearance.@zoomHint: Settings → Zoom, on Windows and Linux; {mod} is the Ctrl key's name, as keycaps show it
appearance.zoomHintMac: Everything bigger or smaller, also with a pinch on the trackpad
appearance.@zoomLevel: Settings → Zoom: accessible name of the button that shows the zoom level and sets it back to normal; {level} is the level, like 125%, {normal} the normal level, 100%
appearance.textSizeHint: How big writing is on pages

textSizes.@small: Settings → Text size: option for smaller writing on pages
textSizes.@default: Settings → Text size: option for the usual size of writing on pages
textSizes.@large: Settings → Text size: option for bigger writing on pages
textSizes.@xlarge: Settings → Text size: option for writing bigger still than Large

sidebar.title: Sidebar
sidebar.@title: Settings: heading of the section that chooses what the sidebar shows

show.@galaxy: Settings → Sidebar: switch for the Galaxy view (every page as a star), like the others in this group

sidebar.note: Hidden ones are still a shortcut or a search away. Right-click an item in the sidebar to hide it from there.

writing.title: Writing
writing.@title: Settings: heading of the section about writing on pages

capture.title: Quick Capture
capture.@title: Settings: heading of the section about Quick Capture, the small window for jotting down a note or to-do (a feature name)
capture.anywhereHint: {shortcut} opens Quick Capture even when Thought Desk is in the background
capture.@anywhereHint: Settings → Quick Capture; {shortcut} is the keys that open it, like Ctrl+Shift+Space
capture.anywhereHintNoShortcut: Its shortcut opens Quick Capture even when Thought Desk is in the background

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.@title: Settings: heading of the section about the calendar
calendar.importHint: Class schedules and due dates from a .ics file (Canvas, Google, Outlook)
calendar.@importButton: Settings → Calendar: button that picks a calendar file to import

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.@title: Settings: heading of the section about reminder notifications
reminders.@assignments: Settings → Reminders: the row that chooses when to be reminded of homework due dates
reminders.assignmentsHint: Plus one an hour before anything with a due time
reminders.@assignmentsOff: Settings → Reminders → Assignments: option for no reminders
reminders.eventsHint: Only events with a start time
reminders.@eventsOff: Settings → Reminders → Before events: option for no reminders
reminders.@minutes: Settings → Reminders → Before events: an option, how many minutes before an event to be reminded (short, it's on a small button); {count} is the number of minutes

courses.title: Courses
courses.@title: Settings: heading of the list of school courses
courses.@assignmentCount: Settings → Courses: under a course's name, how many assignments it has; {count} is the number
courses.empty: Courses group assignments and events and give them a color.

storage.title: Storage
storage.@title: Settings: heading of the section about where and how notes are kept on this computer
storage.@pages: Settings → Storage: how many pages there are, a big number with a word under it; <num> is the number, <noun> the word (keep both tags, no space needed between them); {count} is the number
storage.@assignments: Settings → Storage: how many homework assignments there are, a big number with a word under it; <num> is the number, <noun> the word (keep both tags, no space needed between them); {count} is the number
storage.@events: Settings → Storage: how many calendar events there are, a big number with a word under it; <num> is the number, <noun> the word (keep both tags, no space needed between them); {count} is the number
storage.@files: Settings → Storage: how many files there are, a big number with a word under it; <num> is the number, <noun> the word (keep both tags, no space needed between them); {count} is the number
storage.@size: Settings → Storage: the row that shows how much disk space the notes take
storage.@sizes: Settings → Storage → Size: {database} is the size of the database file, {files} the size of the added files, each like 1.5 MB
storage.@location: Settings → Storage: the row that shows the folder the notes are kept in
storage.@change: Settings → Storage → Location: button that picks another folder to keep the notes in
storage.missingHint: {path} wasn't there when Thought Desk started, so these are the notes in its own folder. Connect the drive and restart, or keep using this folder.
storage.@missingHint: Settings → Storage, when the folder chosen for the notes is missing (an unplugged drive); {path} is that folder's path
storage.exportHint: Every page as a Markdown file, in folders like the sidebar, with databases as CSV and the files they use.
storage.@exportButton: Settings → Storage: button that exports every note to a folder
storage.note: Everything is stored in one SQLite file plus a files folder, in the folder above. Back it up to keep your work safe, or keep it in a folder that's backed up already (Change…).
storage.@note: Settings → Storage, under the section; “Change…” in brackets is the button above that picks another folder (storage.change): write it the same way

about.@version: Settings, at the bottom: the app's name and version; {version} is the version number, like 0.8.0
about.@updating: Settings, at the bottom: shown while an update is downloading
about.@updatingPercent: Settings, at the bottom: shown while an update is downloading; {percent} is how much is done, like 45%
about.@install: Settings, at the bottom: link that installs the new version; {version} is its version number, like 0.9.0
about.@checking: Settings, at the bottom: shown while looking for a new version

keyboard.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
keyboard.intro: Click a shortcut and press new keys. {escape} cancels; {backspace} removes it.
keyboard.@intro: Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts, under the heading; {escape} and {backspace} are those keys' names as keycaps show them (Esc, Backspace)
keyboard.needsModifier: Add {mod} or {alt}, so it doesn’t get in the way of typing
keyboard.@needsModifier: Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts, when the keys pressed have no modifier; {mod} is the main shortcut key (Ctrl, or ⌘ on a Mac), {alt} the Alt key (⌥ on a Mac)
keyboard.@usedFor: Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts, when the keys pressed are kept by the editor or the system; {keys} is the keys, like Ctrl+B, {command} the name of what they do there, like Bold
keyboard.@takenFrom: Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts, after keys were moved here from another command; {command} is that command's name, like Search everything
keyboard.@reset: Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts: accessible name of the button that puts a command's shortcut back to its default; {command} is the command's name
keyboard.@keysLabel: Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts: accessible name of the button showing a command's keys, which records new ones; {command} is the command's name, {keys} its keys, like Ctrl K or Ctrl P
keyboard.@keysLabelNone: Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts: accessible name of the button for a command that has no keys, which records new ones; {command} is the command's name
keyboard.@orKeys: Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts, read out by screen readers: two shortcuts that do the same thing; {first} and {second} are keys, like Ctrl K (with three, {first} is the first two joined)
keyboard.@or: Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts: the small word between two sets of keycaps that do the same thing (Ctrl K or Ctrl P)
keyboard.@none: shown in place of keycaps for a command that has no shortcut

help.markdown: Type at the Start of a Line
help.@typeThenSpace: Keyboard shortcuts sheet: what to type at the start of a line to make a heading, a list…: first {type} (like #), then the Space key; <typed> and <keycap> are drawn as keycaps and <sep> as a small word between them (keep all three tags, no spaces needed between them); {space} is the Space key's name
help.openAnyTime: Open this sheet any time with <kbd>{mod}</kbd><kbd>/</kbd>
help.@openAnyTime: Keyboard shortcuts sheet, at the bottom; <kbd> marks keycaps; {mod} is the main shortcut key (Ctrl, or ⌘ on a Mac)

shortcutGroups.@general: heading over the shortcuts that work everywhere in the app
shortcutGroups.@tabs: heading over the shortcuts for the window's tabs
shortcutGroups.@goTo: heading over the shortcuts that open each view (Home, Calendar…)
shortcutGroups.@calendar: heading over the shortcuts that work in the calendar

commands.@capture: the command that opens Quick Capture, the small window for jotting down a note or to-do (a feature name)
commands.split: Split view (a second page beside this one)
commands.@back: command that goes back to the place shown before
commands.@forward: command that goes forward again after going back
commands.@calendarToday: command that moves the calendar to today's date

editorCommands.@bold: the editor's command that makes text bold
editorCommands.@copy: the command that copies the selection
editorCommands.@italic: the editor's command that makes text italic
editorCommands.@underline: the editor's command that underlines text
editorCommands.@cut: the command that cuts the selection
editorCommands.@redo: the command that does again what was undone
editorCommands.@undo: the command that reverses the last change (Ctrl+Z)
editorCommands.@strikethrough: the editor's command that strikes text through
editorCommands.@highlight: the editor's command that highlights text (a verb)

editorKeys.mention: Link a page, assignment or file
editorKeys.addLink: Add a link to selected text
editorKeys.inlineMathSelection: Inline math (or turn selected text into math)
editorKeys.formula: In a formula: suggestions, next gap, done

markdownKeys.heading: Heading
markdownKeys.@heading: a heading block (a title within a page)
markdownKeys.@checklist: a list of to-dos with checkboxes
markdownKeys.@divider: a horizontal line that divides a page

keys.@escape: the Escape key's name, as printed on keycaps
keys.@delete: the Delete key's name, as printed on keycaps
keys.@backspace: the Backspace key's name, as printed on keycaps
keys.@pageUp: the Page Up key's name, as printed on keycaps
keys.@pageDown: the Page Down key's name, as printed on keycaps
keys.@home: the Home key's name (it goes to the start of a line), as printed on keycaps
keys.@end: the End key's name (it goes to the end of a line), as printed on keycaps
keys.@insert: the Insert key's name, as printed on keycaps
keys.@shift: the Shift key's name, as printed on keycaps
keys.@ctrl: the Control key's name on a Mac keyboard (where ⌘ is the main shortcut key), as printed on keycaps
keys.@tab: the Tab key's name, as printed on keycaps
keys.@enter: the Enter (Return) key's name, as printed on keycaps
keys.@space: the space bar's name, as written on a keycap
keys.@numpad: a key on the number pad, as written on a keycap; {key} is the key, a digit like 0 or 7
keys.@numpadAdd: the + key on the number pad, as written on a keycap
keys.@numpadSubtract: the − key on the number pad, as written on a keycap
keys.@numpadMultiply: the × (*) key on the number pad, as written on a keycap
keys.@numpadDivide: the ÷ (/) key on the number pad, as written on a keycap
keys.@numpadDecimal: the decimal point key on the number pad, as written on a keycap
keys.@numpadEnter: the Enter key on the number pad, as written on a keycap
keys.@numpadEqual: the = key on the number pad, as written on a keycap
keys.@numpadComma: the comma key on the number pad, as written on a keycap

colors.@red: a color's name, on color swatches and in color menus (courses, events, text color)
colors.@orange: a color's name, on color swatches and in color menus (courses, events, text color)
colors.@yellow: a color's name, on color swatches and in color menus (courses, events, text color)
colors.@green: a color's name, on color swatches and in color menus (courses, events, text color)
colors.@teal: a color's name (blue-green), on color swatches and in color menus (courses, events, text color)
colors.@blue: a color's name, on color swatches and in color menus (courses, events, text color)
colors.@indigo: a color's name (deep blue-violet), on color swatches and in color menus (courses, events, text color)
colors.@purple: a color's name, on color swatches and in color menus (courses, events, text color)
colors.@pink: a color's name, on color swatches and in color menus (courses, events, text color)
colors.@gray: a color's name, on color swatches and in color menus (courses, events, text color)
colors.@graphite: the default accent color's name: a near-black gray, like pencil lead

palettes.@default: Settings → Color theme: the app's usual colors (white or black backgrounds)
palettes.@paper: Settings → Color theme: warm off-white backgrounds, like paper
palettes.@slate: Settings → Color theme: cool blue-gray backgrounds, like slate stone
palettes.@sage: Settings → Color theme: soft gray-green backgrounds, like the herb sage
palettes.@rose: Settings → Color theme: soft pink backgrounds
palettes.@dusk: Settings → Color theme: soft violet backgrounds, like the sky at dusk
